verdict.rationale: Each finding carries a confidence score, a source-to-sink call chain, a proof of concept and a suggested patch, which together explain it. An official MCP connection lets an AI tool pull that evidence and triage findings. However, deduplication is not documented; the PR-check separation of new versus pre-existing findings is adjacent, not dedup. False-positive flagging is only implied by the confidence score, and one hands-on user reported two non-real vulnerabilities rated at 100% confidence. Missing for 10: documented deduplication, an explicit false-positive flagging or suppression workflow, a described AI explanation feature beyond the raw evidence, and independent corroboration that the confidence scores are accurate.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can use AI to triage findings — explaining them, deduplicating, and flagging likely false positives

citations.quote: Each finding includes a severity (CVSS 4.0), a confidence score, the full source-to-sink call chain, a proof of concept, and a suggested patch.
Connect it to an AI tool and the tool can list your repositories and scans, pull full vulnerability evidence (proof of concept, call chain, patch diff), triage findings, and file tickets.
